text:
samir: Quick heads-up — hit a consistent repro in the node sampleapp when the client reconnects very quickly (~100-300ms). The stream parser sometimes sees chunks out of order and we get a duplicated final token. Repro steps below.

lena: Can you paste the minimal repro and logs? Is this only Node or JS browser too?

samir: Node only so far. Logs show interleaved fragments after auth refresh. Example snippet I used to stress-reconnect:

```
// repro.js
const es = new EventSource(url);
setTimeout(() => { es.close(); setTimeout(() => new EventSource(url), 150); }, 200);
// loop this a few hundred times
```

samir: Attaching a trimmed log: we see chunk A (partial), auth-refresh, new conn yields chunk B, then remainder of A arrives from old socket -> parser emits B before A's tail -> invalid JSON/final token twice.

jonah: Hmm. Sounds like resume/last-event-id merging race — old socket isn't fully drained before parser switches. We've seen similar on mobile but with different timing.

maria: Could be the SDK's reconnect path that immediately swaps the parser without verifying the prior stream closed. Did you try toggling the SDK's `bufferChunks` option?

samir: Yep tried `bufferChunks: false` and `true`. freq drops with buffering but doesn't go away. On `false` we still saw misorders when auth refresh timestamped in middle of a chunk.

lena: Proposed quick mitigation: add per-chunk sequence tokens (opaque incrementing header) and have client drop any chunk with seq <= lastSeen. That avoids dup/final-token double-emit while we patch reassembly.

jonah: Also add a small wait-for-close window (50ms) before the new parser eats data, but that may increase tail latency. Could gate by `Content-Length` or final delimiter when available.

samir: I'll open a small PR with seq-drop + config flag `strictReassembly` default false. If infra wants to enable later per-customer, we can flip it.

devex-bot: Created issue <https://tracker.redwood.ai/RED-1234|RED-1234> "node sampleapp: reconnect chunk reorder causing duplicate final token" and attached logs.

infra-bot: Note: this might be amplified under high packet reordering or when TCP connections hang in CLOSE_WAIT on the server side. I'll put a quick note on the infra runbook.

maria: For the longer term we should audit the auth refresh hook: it currently calls `abort()` which could leave a partially-parsed buffer. Maybe we should signal `finishSegment` before abort.

lena: Agreed. Short-term: seq-drop PR + e2e in sampleapp CI that artificially reconnects with randomized delays. Long-term: parser rework to support chunk-fragment assembly across reconnects when `Last-Event-Id`/resume present.

samir: I'll push the PR this afternoon and include a small repro harness (looped EventSource). Assigning reviewers: @lena and @jonah. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

lena: Thanks — please include a comment in the PR linking to RED-1234 and the sampleapp CI job name so we can track flakiness.

jonah: I'll add a lib-level unit test for fragment reassembly after auth refresh once PR lands.

samir: Cool. If anyone can try the repro locally and confirm before I merge that'd be great. I'm dropping the script in `devex/sampleapp/repro/reconnect-misorder.js`.
